Resolves #18764
Refs #18762

`Neo.grid.plugin.CellEditing` no longer extends the Table plugin. It owns one logical edit session, `{recordId, dataField, editor}`, and `grid.Row#applyRendererOutput` embeds that editor in whichever pooled cell renders the session, on every render. A scroll that keeps the cell keeps the editor and its focus. A row rebind or a column leaving the mounted window suspends the editor with its App Worker draft intact, and the next render reprojects it. Double-click, Enter and F2 start an edit; Enter commits and Escape cancels; focus leaving the grid or activating another cell commits a valid draft. `grid.column.Base` declares `editable_` and `editor`.

Evidence: L3 (real-browser component and Brain-free e2e arms in CI, plus local red-on-dev, mutation and CPU-throttle runs) → L3 required (AC-2 to AC-9 are browser-observable). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the PR body and file-size guards ran.

| AC-1 | `src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs` extends `Neo.plugin.Base`; `git grep -n "table/plugin/CellEditing" src/grid` is empty; `docs/output/class-hierarchy.json` is regenerated |
| AC-2 | CI components `grid/CellEditing.spec.mjs` › activation (double-click and throttled double-click per body, Enter and F2, Space and non-editable start nothing); CI e2e `grid/CellEditingPooling.spec.mjs` › double-click per pooled body |
| AC-3 | CI components › terminals (Enter writes a valid dirty draft, Escape discards and destroys the editor, an invalid draft blocks Enter); CI e2e › Escape and Enter while a body render is in the air |
| AC-4 | CI e2e › horizontal remap / leaving the window / returning restores the draft; vertical rebind suspends and reprojects |
| AC-5 | CI components › one session (activating another cell commits first with one editor at a time; focus leaving the grid commits) |
| AC-6 | CI components › turning editable off on the active column cancels its session |
| AC-7 | CI e2e › navigation keys pressed inside the editor never scroll the View (caret semantics asserted where Home/End bind to the caret) |
| AC-8 | CI components › a click inside the editor keeps focus in it and leaves the cell selection alone; red with the `onRowClick` exemption removed (mutation below) |
| AC-9 | CI components › teardown (destroying the grid; destroying the plugin alone); red with either cleanup removed (mutation below) |
| AC-10 | Both specs run in CI tiers; `node buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs --coverage-line`: 21 of 113 on dev → 22 of 114 at head |

## Deltas from ticket
- **Selection repaint** (`src/selection/Model.mjs`, `src/selection/grid/BaseModel.mjs`). `deselect`/`deselectAll` now honor `view.silentSelect`, and the grid model restores the flag through `silently()` instead of resetting it. A single-select `select()` runs `deselectAll()` inside, and that reset re-enabled a whole-View update on every cell click. The View flight overlapped the Row flights, which applied the editor's `insertNode` twice. The editable-off arm pins it.
- **Drag scroll** (`src/main/addon/GridDragScroll.mjs`). A drag starting in `.neo-grid-editor` selects text instead of scrolling the grid, pinned by an e2e drag arm.
- **Home/End platform** reads `navigator.platform`. Playwright device emulation spoofs `userAgentData.platform`, while key bindings follow the host OS.
- **Focus follows the editor's own mount**, not the repaint promise. A Row render in flight settles a `promiseUpdate()` requested during it. That engine defect is out of scope, noted in the VdomLifecycle defect-note. With it gone, the session no longer needs D#17832's `generation`.
- **The editor is destroyed through its Row** (`destroy(true, true)`), which CI found for me: a body render collected before the edit ended landed afterwards, walked the live Row reference into the vnode the Row keeps, and failed on the retired editor's name. That unlink is the engine's own retired-reference handling, and `editor.destroy()`'s defaults skip it.
- **AC-9 plugin-only destroy:** no production caller destroys the plugin alone, and the arm that pins it found two real defects in CI. A plugin destroyed while its grid lives now ends the edit through `cancelEdit()`, so the cell is repainted instead of keeping an input nothing owns; a grid being destroyed keeps the short path, since its store and bodies are already gone.
- **The fixture's small grid declares the plugin with an id**, which CI also found: the generated `neo-plugin-grid-cell-editing-1` names whichever of the two grids constructed its plugin first, and that order comes from two dynamic imports of one module. `#grid-cell-editing-pooled` keeps `cellEditing: true`, so the public entry point and its lazy import stay covered by the e2e arms.
- **Test harness:** the component spec uses the shared fixtures, so a worker error fails an arm. `isLive` races a second `getConfigs` because falsy worker replies do not settle on main before #18768. The `RowCellIdMigration` Row fake gains `getPlugin`.

## Test Evidence
- **Red on dev** (new specs copied onto `e197300297`): components 17/17 red and e2e 7/7 red. Every arm fails at its first editor poll, because the inherited plugin embodies nothing.
- **Mutations**, each red on its owning arm:
  - `onRowClick` editor guard: AC-8 arm.
  - `onCellClick` editor guard.
  - `DomEvents` navigation-key suppression: e2e keys arm.
  - `GridDragScroll` editor exclusion: e2e drag arm.
  - `isEmbodied` classification: horizontal and vertical arms.
  - BaseModel `silently()` restore: editable-off arm, `Expected: 1, Received: 2` editors inserted.
  - Plugin `removeKeys`: plugin-destroy arm, `pageerror: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'onEnterKey')`.
  - Editor destroyed with `destroy()`'s defaults instead of through the Row: both in-flight arms, 6/6, with the CI error verbatim.
  - **Not locally discriminating, stated as such:** removing the plugin-destroy repaint passes 6/6 here, because a focus-driven render happens to remove the orphaned input within the arm's wait. CI is where it reds, twice (jobs 104752123499 and its predecessor), which is why the fix landed at all.
- **In-flight destruction:** a 1px scroll followed at once by Escape reproduced CI's `vdom update failed … Component not found for id: neo-textfield-1` 11/12 locally, and 12/12 green after the fix. Both directions are now arms.
- **Focus race:** at 8x CPU throttle the double-click arms went 9/9 red at `c638681ce8` and 9/9 green at `73c317752d`. A main-thread trace showed the focus call arriving before the editor node.
- **Brain-gated grid e2e**, which CI deselects: `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=… npm run test-e2e -- test/playwright/e2e/grid` gives 41/41. That includes `GridViewFocus` and `SelectionMultiBody`, which cover the selection and row-click changes.
- **Regression:** the full components tier and the unit grid, selection, list, table, plugin, menu and form dirs, `main/DomEvents` and `main/addon/GridDragScroll` all pass. One exception: `selection/GalleryInternalId` fails when it shares a worker with `main/DomEvents.spec`, and does so identically on dev.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Finding — `selection.Model#deselectAll` loses its emptiness guard, and the sibling site keeps it.**

```diff
-            if (!silent && items.length > 0) {
+            if (!silent && !view.silentSelect) {
                 view.update()
             }
```

The `silentSelect` half is right and needed. Dropping `items.length > 0` is the part I am holding on: `deselectAll()` over an already-empty selection now calls `view.update()` where it previously returned without rendering — for **every** list, table and grid, since `selection.Model` is the base.

The evidence that it is collateral rather than intended is in the same file. `restoreSelection` (`:344`) reads:

```js
if (me.items.length > 0) {
    ...
    if (!silent && !view.silentSelect) {
        view.update()
    }
}
```

Emptiness guard **and** silentSelect guard, nested. So the established pattern is both, not one instead of the other — which is exactly what the replacement makes it look like. Grid is unaffected (your `silently()` sets `silentSelect` across the call), so this lands on the consumers the ticket does not touch.

**What I actively looked for and cleared:**

- **A pool slot carrying the editor for the wrong record.** The projection keys on `{recordId, dataField}` *and* reparents to the rendering Row, so a rebinding that drops the cell unmounts the editor rather than orphaning it. The ticket's first Avoided Trap, closed structurally.
- **`silently()` masking a reset bug rather than fixing one.** It fixes one: the old `view.silentSelect = false` was a *reset*, and your docblock names the case that breaks — single-select `select()` runs `deselectAll()` first, so the inner reset re-enabled View updates for the rest of the outer change. Save-and-restore in a `try/finally` is the correct shape and the reason is written where the next reader meets it.
- **An undeclared config, the defect this ticket exists partly to fix.** `silentSelect` is declared at `list/Base.mjs:163`; `editable_` and `editor` are now declared with JSDoc, matching the Ledger row that called them out as undeclared today.
- **The main-thread guard over-reaching.** It is triple-gated — `tagName === 'INPUT'`, the key set, and `testPathInclusion(['neo-grid-editor'])` — and Home/End are additionally gated on `/Mac/.test(navigator.platform)`, which is the ticket's stated reason (bindings follow the host OS) rather than a blanket suppression. `neo-table-editor` is untouched, as the Ledger says.

**Merge-order note, not a required action:** this branch points at `d486a03a8d` and `origin/dev` has moved three merges since — including #18766 (`17f5a83b95`), which **adds a block to the same `onKeyDown` method**. `git diff origin/dev..HEAD` therefore renders that block as a deletion; it is a stale-base artifact, not something your diff removes, and GitHub reports `MERGEABLE`. Worth a re-check at the merge gate anyway, since same-method edits from two branches are where a clean auto-merge and a correct result diverge.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit (per guide §7.4):**

- [x] The class docblock's *"the Row, not the plugin, decides where an edit is visible"* is literally what `applyRendererOutput` does.
